analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction with the app repeatedly crashing at login and says she suffered material inconvenience: she could not pay her rent on time and had to travel to a branch 40 minutes away. This meets CH-1.
analysis.summary: The customer reports that the Harbourline app has crashed every time she tries to log in over the last three weeks. This is her fourth call about the same issue. Earlier agents advised a reinstall and clearing the cache. An IT ticket may have been raised on 2026-10-13, but it is not confirmed that it was sent. Because of the fault she could not pay her rent on time and had to travel 40 minutes to a branch. She wants the app fixed and compensation for the hassle. She uses an Android phone; the app version is unknown. No financial loss amount is stated. Late rent may point to possible financial strain, which has not been explored.

timeline.event: First call: app crashes at login. Agent advised reinstalling the app.
Second call: app still crashing. Agent advised clearing the cache.
Third call: still crashing after reinstall. Agent may have raised an IT ticket; not sure if it was sent.
Customer could not pay her rent on time and went to a branch 40 minutes away.
Fourth call. Logged as a complaint. Android phone, app version unknown.

analysis.severity_reason: This is a repeated service failure: the customer has contacted the bank four times about the same issue, which meets the Medium threshold in CH-6. No financial loss is quantified. Severity should be reconsidered if late rent caused a charge, if the customer is vulnerable and at risk of harm, or if the crash is affecting many customers (systemic).

vulnerability.suggested_support: This is a possible indicator only. Her inability to pay rent on time was caused by the app fault, but it may also reflect tight finances. Ask the customer sensitively whether she needs any support and whether the late rent caused any charges or hardship. Offer reasonable adjustments, such as phone contact on [PHONE_1] and help to make payments while the app is unavailable. Note that note_4 says no indicators were mentioned, but the customer was not asked.

analysis.routing_reason: A persistent app login crash over three weeks, which basic troubleshooting has not fixed, needs technical investigation by Digital Operations under ESC-1. The IT ticket status is uncertain. If the investigation finds the fault affects many customers, Senior Complaints Review should also be considered. The complaints handler remains the point of contact under ESC-5 and decides any redress under CH-8.
